statement: A polynomial $P(x)$ has integer coefficients and $P(2) = 7$. Which of the following could be the value of $P(9)$?

choices.misconception: I thought P(9) - P(2) had to be divisible by 9 times 2 = 18, and 25 - 7 = 18.
I thought P(9) - P(2) only had to be divisible by the larger input 9, and 34 - 7 = 27.
I thought P(9) - P(2) had to be divisible by 9 + 2 = 11, and 40 - 7 = 33.
I mixed up the input 2 with the output 7 and checked whether P(9) - 2 is a multiple of 7, and 44 - 2 = 42.

hints: For each power, $9^k - 2^k$ is divisible by $9 - 2$. So $9 - 2$ divides $P(9) - P(2)$.
$P(9) - 7$ must be a multiple of $7$. Test each choice, then build a polynomial for the one that passes.

solutions.reliable: Write $P(x) = \sum c_k x^k$ with integer $c_k$. Then $P(9) - P(2) = \sum c_k (9^k - 2^k)$, and each $9^k - 2^k$ is divisible by $9 - 2 = 7$. So $P(9) \equiv P(2) = 7 \equiv 0 \pmod 7$, meaning $P(9)$ must be a multiple of $7$. Among the choices only $21$ is. It is achieved by $P(x) = 2x + 3$: $P(2) = 7$ and $P(9) = 21$.
solutions.elegant: Since $9 \equiv 2 \pmod 7$, any polynomial with integer coefficients gives $P(9) \equiv P(2) \pmod 7$. The others, $25, 34, 40, 44$, leave remainders $4, 6, 5, 2$, so only $21$ works.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
